text:
miles: Weird one from dogfood: our containerized onboarding demo used the org key after we rotated a project key in k8s. Repro notes below.

miles: repro: app runs in a Docker image that sources secret files under /run/secrets (REDWOOD_API_KEY) and k8s injects RW_API_KEY_PROJECT as an env var via Deployment. After the k8s secret update (rotation) we saw requests billed to the org key.

miles: quick log excerpt: `startup: exported /run/secrets/REDWOOD_API_KEY -> REDWOOD_API_KEY=org-zzzz`, then `auth: selected=REDWOOD_API_KEY (org-zzzz)` even though RW_API_KEY_PROJECT=proj-3333 is present in env.

harper: I think two things collided: entrypoint script that exports files to env runs before k8s env injection is fully visible in some sidecar scenarios, and our SDK loader treats file-backed REDWOOD_API_KEY as higher priority than RW_API_KEY_PROJECT. Also kubelet mounts update atomically and sometimes containers see old file contents until restart.

carmen: Also saw this in CI where the rotator job updates a secret, mounts are refreshed, but our image-level entrypoint caches the key in a file and doesn't re-evaluate at runtime. So rotation without container restart leaves stale auth.

harper: Minimal repro (local):
```
# simulate file-backed legacy key
printf 'org-aaaa' > /tmp/redwood_key
export REDWOOD_API_KEY_FILE=/tmp/redwood_key
export RW_API_KEY_PROJECT=proj-3333
node sampleapp.js
# logs show REDWOOD_API_KEY used
```

carmen: Two separate UX fixes proposed: 1) env/file precedence rules documented and enforced in loader (prefer most-specific scoped keys regardless of source: RW_API_KEY_PROJECT_file > RW_API_KEY_PROJECT_env > RW_API_KEY_SERVICE > REDWOOD_API_KEY_file > REDWOOD_API_KEY_env); 2) support optional file-watch or SIGHUP-triggered reload so file-backed secrets can refresh without full container restart.

miles: +1. Also add a one-time WARN when both a REDWOOD_API_KEY file and RW_API_KEY_PROJECT env exist, because that's an easy silent mis-bill. Produce a masked diag line at startup showing selected source and tail (e.g., "auth.selected=RW_API_KEY_PROJECT_env (****3333)").

harper: For long-lived streams: when a file-backed key changes mid-connection we should attempt a refresh: call tokenProvider.refresh() or re-read secret file, swap auth header and retry the failed frame once. If still 401 -> emit `auth.rotation_failed` event. Avoid tight loops.

carmen: Implementation plan: small non-breaking change in SDK loader:
- introduce explicit precedence order (most-specific first) and check both env and file variants for each key name;
- emit WARN+telemetry when legacy file/env coexist with scoped RW_API_KEY_*;
- add opt-in file-watch support behind RW_ENABLE_FILE_RELOAD=true;
- add RW_LEGACY_KEY_COMPAT=true to preserve old behavior for one release.

k8s-bot: created issue https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/issues/2244 "sdk: file/env precedence + k8s secret rotation + stream refresh"

ci-runner: I can add a CI matrix job that mounts secrets as files and as envs and runs the rotation e2e (simulate file update, assert SDK picks scoped key or emits warn).

miles: Action items: carmen open PR to change loader and add diag/warn; harper prototype SIGHUP reload and file-watch; ci-runner add CI e2e; i'll update onboarding docs with a k8s section recommending not to mount REDWOOD_API_KEY when using project keys.

harper: small note: prefer suffix naming RW_API_KEY_PROJECT to keep RW_API_KEY_* namespace consistent for auto-complete in tooling.

miles: thanks all. prioritize the WARN+doc so we don't silently misbill, then follow with file-reload and stream refresh. Closing until PRs land.
